words.sense: deviating from conventional, normal, or accepted social behavior and habits in an odd, whimsical, or idiosyncratic manner without being harmful
words.concise_meaning: unconventional and slightly strange in behavior, habits, or appearance, though not malicious or dangerous
words.connotation: mildly amused, tolerant, affectionate, colorful, non-judgmental
words.grammar: adjective; used attributively ('an eccentric inventor') or predicatively ('his habits were eccentric')
misconceptions: Assuming that eccentric implies madness, psychosis, or dangerous hostility, rather than harmless, idiosyncratic departure from conventional norms.

words.sense: selecting, combining, or drawing ideas, styles, tastes, or methods from a broad and diverse range of varied sources
words.concise_meaning: deriving ideas, style, or taste from a broad, diverse range of sources, systems, or historical traditions
words.connotation: positive to analytical, sophisticated, open-minded, cultivated
words.grammar: adjective; used attributively ('an eclectic mix', 'eclectic taste') or predicatively ('her musical taste is eclectic')
misconceptions: Believing that eclectic simply means weird, messy, or disorganized, forgetting that it specifically requires drawing from a variety of distinct traditions, genres, or sources.

semantic_axes.description: Deriving elements from a variety of distinct external traditions, systems, or genres (eclectic) vs. departing from conventional norms through peculiar, individualized personal habits or quirks (eccentric).
Synthesizing heterogeneous inputs into a composite whole (eclectic) vs. deviating off-center from standard social expectations and practices (eccentric).

Applied primarily to taste, collections, methodologies, intellectual frameworks, and aesthetics (eclectic) vs. applied primarily to conduct, mannerisms, personal rituals, and individual lifestyles (eccentric).

edge.boundary_rule: Eclectic describes selecting, blending, or drawing from a wide variety of diverse sources, styles, or traditions; eccentric describes deviating from conventional norms through peculiar, unusual, or idiosyncratic behavior, habits, or character.
clues_a: unconventional personal rituals or bizarre daily habits
harmlessly flouting ordinary social customs and decorum
peculiar individual mannerisms lacking multi-source origins
odd, whimsical lifestyle choices driven by private whims
deviating off-center from accepted behavioral standards
clues_b: borrowing techniques or motifs from multiple distinct cultures or historical eras
curating an ensemble or collection from heterogeneous origins
synthesizing diverse intellectual, artistic, or culinary traditions
selecting the best elements across disparate disciplines or genres
broad variety of stylistic inputs integrated into one body of work
irrelevant_clues: how visually striking, colorful, or surprising the result appears
the personal wealth, academic status, or fame of the actor
whether the outcome is deemed artistic, chaotic, or polished
the age or monetary value of the objects involved

misconceptions.M1: Confusing multi-source variety with personal oddity — calling a diverse synthesis eccentric simply because the combination is rare or striking.
misconceptions.M2: Assuming any bizarre habit or isolated quirk is eclectic, ignoring that eclectic strictly requires drawing from varied sources or traditions.
misconceptions.M3: Viewing eccentric as dangerous, malicious, or deranged, rather than a harmless and colorful departure from standard social norms.

eccentric: The retired colonel walks his pet lobster on a leash through the village market every morning at dawn.
She wears a velvet top hat filled with fresh parsley to board meetings and insists on being addressed as Admiral.
He refuses to enter rooms through doorways, climbing through ground-floor windows even in formal dinner attire.
The mathematician writes his formulas exclusively on dried autumn leaves stored in cardboard shoeboxes.
She sleeps exclusively in a wooden rowing boat suspended from her living room ceiling.
The hermit pays his utility bills using antique silver coins wrapped inside handwritten rhyming riddles.
eclectic: Her private art collection features Japanese woodblock prints, Soviet space race posters, and West African bronze figurines.
The restaurant menu combines Peruvian ceviche, Ethiopian sourdough injera, and classical French pastry.
His dissertation methodology synthesizes quantitative statistical modeling, Marxist historical critique, and indigenous oral tradition analysis.
The DJ's evening set seamlessly blends 1970s funk, classical cello concertos, and modern Detroit techno beats.
Their home decor brings together Victorian velvet armchairs, Scandinavian pine benches, and industrial metal factory lamps.
The curriculum for the new seminar draws readings from ancient Greek philosophy, Buddhist sutras, and contemporary cognitive science.

eccentric: The music festival's lineup features traditional Irish folk, Afrobeat percussion, Brazilian samba, and electronic ambient soundscapes.
His architectural portfolio combines Spanish colonial archways, modern minimalist glass walls, and rustic alpine stonework.
The university reading list gathers historical texts from ancient Chinese Confucianism, medieval European scholasticism, and pre-colonial African governance.
Her fashion line integrates Scandinavian wool-knitting techniques, Japanese indigo dye methods, and vibrant Guatemalan weaves.
The chef's spice cabinet gathers blends from Turkish bazaars, Indian spice markets, Caribbean islands, and Mexican mountain villages.
The documentary soundtrack assembles Renaissance choral singing, Delta blues acoustic guitar, and contemporary Berlin synthesizer drones.
eclectic: The wealthy recluse carries a yellow umbrella indoors at all times to shield his head from ceiling lamps.
He eats his meals solely while standing on his head against the dining room wall.
She dresses exclusively in layers of aluminum foil whenever rain is forecast in the city.
The inventor refuses to ride in vehicles unless he is permitted to pedal an unattached bicycle gear on his lap.
He communicates with his neighbors solely through handwritten limericks tossed over the garden fence in plastic bottles.
She keeps twelve grandfather clocks in her bedroom, each set to ring thirty seconds apart throughout the night.
